headline: Malaysia to recruit 2 lakh Bangladeshi workers starting September
summary: 10,000 workers will be recruited free of cost, according to State Minister for Local Government, Mir Shah Alam.
details: The Malaysian government will recruit approximately 2 lakh Bangladeshi workers through various recruiting agencies, starting in September.
State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam announced this following a meeting with the Malaysian Ambassador at the Secretariat on Sunday.
As part of the agreement, 10,000 of these workers will be recruited free of cost.
Beyond labor recruitment, Malaysia will provide technical assistance to Bangladesh for road construction using rubber-mixed bitumen technology to ensure road durability.
Malaysia has also committed to cooperating with Bangladesh in the renewable energy sector.
Separately, the State Minister mentioned that rickshaws will be banned from the main roads of the capital city, as laws have already been enacted.
Two and four-seater e-rickshaws will be brought under registration, while six-seater e-rickshaws will be banned in Dhaka and only available for registration in other urban areas.

Separately, the State Minister mentioned that rickshaws will be banned from the main roads of the capital city, as laws have already been enacted.

headline_marked: Two arrested after [[headteacher dies in mugging]] near Parliament
headline: Two arrested after headteacher dies in mugging near Parliament
summary: Ronjila Parvin, a primary school headteacher from Bogura, died after falling from a rickshaw when muggers pulled her bag in Dhaka.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested two suspects, including the prime suspect, in connection with the death of a primary school headteacher.
The victim, Ronjila Parvin, was the headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogura. She had come to Dhaka with her husband to consult a doctor at Farmgate.
The incident occurred around 6:30 am yesterday near the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Two muggers on a motorcycle pulled at her bag, causing her to fall from the rickshaw.
Ronjila suffered severe head injuries and a fractured spine from the fall. She was declared dead at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital.
The victim's husband, Abdul Matin, witnessed the entire incident and later filed a murder case with the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station.
The arrestees have been identified as Poni, also known as Para Poni, and one of his associates. RAB will hold a press briefing regarding the arrests.
caption:
A primary school headteacher died after falling from a rickshaw during a mugging attempt in front of the Parliament complex.

Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested two suspects, including the prime suspect, in connection with the death of a primary school headteacher.

The victim, Ronjila Parvin, was the headteacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogura. She had come to Dhaka with her husband to consult a doctor at Farmgate.

The incident occurred around 6:30 am yesterday near the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Two muggers on a motorcycle pulled at her bag, causing her to fall from the rickshaw.

Ronjila suffered severe head injuries and a fractured spine from the fall. She was declared dead at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital.

The victim's husband, Abdul Matin, witnessed the entire incident and later filed a murder case with the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station.

The arrestees have been identified as Poni, also known as Para Poni, and one of his associates. RAB will hold a press briefing regarding the arrests.
